entities.span: Fix the known problems in the incoming listing data rather than switching sources: the same job appearing under different identifiers, escaped characters reaching the reader as literal text, a salary rendered as a range from a number to itself, and occasional ungrounded outlier figures. Two problems, not one: incoming source text needs **normalising** as well as de-duplicating, a widening recorded 2026-09-16 rather than the original framing.
The dedup key is the risky part: key on the wrong field and a genuinely different real result disappears silently.
**Done when:** genuine duplicates collapse into one result while two distinct roles at the same company stay distinct,
no escape sequence from the source reaches the reader as literal characters,
a single salary figure renders as a figure rather than a fake range,
outliers are handled visibly rather than shown as fact,
and the dedup key is exercised by a test that would fail if it hid a real result.

One **Done when** clause is already met, ahead of this feature's own design. "A single salary figure renders as a figure rather than a fake range" was closed on 2026-09-13 by [#130](https://github.com/ghalynho10/JobHunt/pull/130) (the equal salary minimum and maximum fix): `salaryText` in `src/lib/listing-format.ts` returns one formatted figure when the two are equal, which fixes `/search` and `/applications` together because both screens format pay through that one helper. **The other three clauses are untouched and this feature stays unstarted.**
rejected_spans: and spec 0013 AC-8, which says "a salary range when present", had simply never considered the equal case, so no spec changed.

entities.span: The comparison is on the raw numbers, so two figures differing by cents still format identically under `maximumFractionDigits: 0` and still render as a range of one figure to itself (verified 2026-09-13: `salaryMin: 109440.2` with `salaryMax: 109440.4` returns `$109,440 to $109,440`), which is reachable because `src/features/search/adzuna.ts` parses both figures as `z.number()` and not as an integer.
Whether to close that by comparing the formatted strings rather than the raw numbers is undecided and belongs to this feature's design. Decide it here rather than inheriting an answer.
rejected_spans: For: at `maximumFractionDigits: 0` the difference is already invisible, so a range of one figure to itself reveals nothing a single figure would hide, and "do these two render identically" is the question the display is actually asking. Against: a range at least signals that the source supplied two values, where one figure asserts it supplied one.

entities.span: **Escaped newlines render as literal text.** Adzuna returns the two character sequence `\n` inside the description field and the app prints it verbatim, seen on a PNC listing. Nothing normalises it: `src/features/search/adzuna.ts` parses the field as a plain string (`descriptionSnippet: raw.description`, verified 2026-09-16) and every screen renders that value directly (`/search`, `/applications` and `/demo`, verified 2026-09-16).

It is also **stored, not only displayed**: applying copies the snippet onto the application row as `job_description` (`src/features/applications/queries.ts`), so a listing captured today keeps the literal characters after the posting is gone, and fixing the render alone would leave every already saved row wrong.
the design should settle the general rule (which escape sequences, decoded or stripped, and at the parse boundary or at render) rather than special casing this one sequence.
rejected_spans: This is the clause that widens the feature from de-duplication to normalisation,

entities.span: **One posting, two Adzuna ids.** The same posting comes back under two different `id` values, so de-duplication keyed on `source_job_id` does not collapse them; seen twice for Everpure. This is the failure mode the intent above already predicted, now confirmed on real data, and it says something the prediction did not: the identifier is the wrong key on its own.
Whatever replaces or supplements it is exactly the risky call this feature's **Done when** asks to be proved by a test.
